reason: The text presents multiple regular human characters with direct speech and expressed emotions/opinions. Rahab (רָחָב) is the central character who speaks extensively, expressing her knowledge that God has given the land to Israel (יָדַעְתִּי כִּֽי־ נָתַן יְהוָה לָכֶם אֶת־ הָאָרֶץ), her fear about the inhabitants' courage melting (וְכִֽי־ נָפְלָה אֵֽימַתְכֶם עָלֵינוּ), and her emotional concern for her family's safety. The two spies (שְׁנַֽיִם־ אֲנָשִׁים) receive commands, hide, negotiate, and report. Joshua sends them with instructions. The King of Jericho issues orders. All these characters have named roles, direct speech lines, and demonstrate emotional responses and reasoned positions throughout the narrative.
